suggestions.reason: No assertion checks whether the reply honours the user's recorded instruction 'pick a default and we'll revisit' / 'I don't want a config knob for everything'. The with_skill reply declines to pick a number and asks a question instead; the baseline picks invented numbers. Which behaviour the skill author wants is an important outcome the current assertions leave ungraded, and the 'no invented numbers' assertion pulls against the user quote.

suggestions.assertion: The first paragraph names the pick and a reason tied to the project (the partner burst incident), not a generic trade-off
suggestions.reason: 'First paragraph' is ambiguous when the reply leads with a one-line 'Token bucket.' followed by bullets (as the baseline does). Consider rewording to 'the pick and a project-tied reason appear before any generic algorithm comparison'.

suggestions.assertion: The reply does not restate decisions NOTES.md already settles (Redis, 429, per-key) as if new
suggestions.reason: Passes for both runs easily; a reply that mentions Redis/429/per-key as background still passes. Consider tightening to 'does not justify or recommend Redis, 429, or per-key keying' so it fails only when the model re-argues them.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven pass and the evidence is substantive, but the baseline also passes six, so this eval currently discriminates on one assertion (invented default numbers). Adding an assertion about handling 'pick a default' and the open bucket-size question would separate the two runs more meaningfully.
